status: DRAFT v0.1: not yet reviewed, pretested or calibrated.
notes: GLOBAL = engagement with allies and institutions; HAWK = willingness to use force and military strength. They are expected to correlate weakly; the pilot tests the split. Items tagged 'current' (Israel, Ukraine) are a rotating module and are excluded from axis scores if they drift.

items.stem: Which comes closer to your view of the US role in the world?
items.scope: Think about the long run, not one conflict.

sides.label: Active role
sides.text: Take an active role in world affairs, even if it is costly and risks war.

sides.label: Focus at home
sides.text: Focus on problems at home and stay out of other countries' affairs, even if rivals gain influence.

items.stem: When pursuing its goals abroad, which should the US usually do?
items.scope: Think about trade, security and diplomacy.

sides.label: Work with allies
sides.text: Work through alliances and agreements, even if that means compromising sometimes.

sides.label: Act alone if needed
sides.text: Act on its own to pursue its interests, even if allies object.

items.stem: Should the US remain in NATO, the military alliance with Canada and most of Europe?
items.scope: Members promise to defend each other if attacked.
options: Yes, and strengthen the US commitment
Yes, but require allies to spend much more on defense
Yes, but reduce US forces in Europe

items.stem: Should US military spending go up or down?
items.scope: Today it is roughly $900 billion a year, more than the next several countries combined.
options: Cut it by a quarter or more

facts.claim: US national defense spending roughly $850-950 billion per year (FY2025-26); exceeds the next ~9 countries combined
facts.source: CBO; SIPRI Military Expenditure Database; Peter G. Peterson Foundation

items.stem: Should the US keep troops stationed in other countries, like Germany, Japan and South Korea?
items.scope: Permanent bases in allied countries, not war zones.

items.stem: Would you support using US military force in each of these situations?
items.scope: Assume Congress or the UN has not acted. Answer each case separately.

cases.text: To stop a government from killing large numbers of its own people
To stop a hostile country from building nuclear weapons
To protect international shipping from attacks
To rescue Americans held hostage abroad
To strike drug cartels in another country without that country's permission

items.stem: Should US spending on foreign aid go up or down?
items.scope: Economic, health and humanitarian aid, not military aid.
items.context: Before 2025 cuts, foreign aid was about 1% of the federal budget.

facts.claim: US foreign aid historically about 1% of federal outlays

items.stem: Should the US fund programs abroad that fight diseases like HIV, malaria and childhood illness?
items.scope: Programs run by US agencies or through charities.
options: End funding; that's for other countries to handle

items.stem: Should the US provide military aid to Israel?
items.scope: Weapons and funding for Israel's military.
options: Yes, with conditions on how weapons are used
Only defensive weapons, like missile defense
items.notes: Rotating 'current' module. Expected to cross-cut G (opposition on parts of both left and right).

items.stem: Should the US support creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel?
items.scope: A state in the West Bank and Gaza.
options: Yes, and push hard for it now
Yes, but only after a negotiated peace with security guarantees for Israel

items.stem: If fighting between Russia and Ukraine continues or resumes, what should the US do?
items.scope: Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.
options: Increase military aid to help Ukraine win back its territory
Give enough aid for Ukraine to defend itself, while pushing for talks
End most aid and press Ukraine to accept a settlement
End all aid and stay out
items.notes: Rotating 'current' module; check the state of the war before each release.

items.stem: If China invaded Taiwan, what should the US do?
items.scope: Taiwan is a self-governing island that China claims.
options: Send weapons and impose sanctions, but no US troops
Send US forces to defend Taiwan

items.stem: Which comes closest to how the US should deal with China?
items.scope: Think about the overall relationship over the next decade.
options: Cooperate on shared problems and avoid confrontation
Compete economically, but keep talking and cooperate where possible
Treat China as the main adversary and confront it on all fronts

items.stem: How should the US deal with the United Nations?
items.scope: The UN and its agencies.
options: Give it more power and funding
Stay in and pay the full US share
Stay in, but cut funding and take part less

items.stem: Should the US accept the authority of the International Criminal Court, which tries people for war crimes?
items.scope: The US is not a member today.
options: Yes, join and accept its authority
Cooperate case by case, without joining
Don't join, and punish the court when it targets Americans or US allies

facts.claim: The US signed but did not ratify the Rome Statute and withdrew its signature in 2002; sanctions on ICC officials imposed in 2020 and 2025

items.stem: Which comes closer to how the US should treat countries with poor human rights records?
items.scope: Countries that jail critics or persecute minorities.

sides.label: Press on rights
sides.text: Press them on human rights, even if it hurts trade or security ties.

sides.label: Interests first
sides.text: Work with them when it serves US interests, whatever their record.

items.stem: Should the US negotiate limits on nuclear weapons with Russia and China?
items.scope: Agreements that cap or reduce each country's arsenal.
options: Yes, aiming for sharp cuts and eventually none
Yes, mutual limits while keeping a strong arsenal
No; build up US nuclear forces without limits

items.stem: Should young Americans be required to serve their country?
items.scope: In peacetime, for people aged about 18 to 25.
options: No requirement, but strong rewards like college aid
Yes, a year of military or civilian service for everyone
Yes, required military service for everyone

items.stem: Should the US use drone strikes against leaders of terrorist groups in other countries?
items.scope: Groups that have attacked or threatened Americans.
options: Only with the other country's permission

items.stem: Which countries should the US sell weapons to?
items.scope: Sales by US companies that the government approves.
options: Only close allies that are democracies
Friendly countries, but not those with poor human rights records
